transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-02 14:00 PDT | Duration: 55 mins | Attendees: Sam Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Miguel (CTO), Aisha (ML Eng), Daniel (Product), Lina (Security)

Summary (auto): quick discovery focused on model selection for a multilingual, tool-heavy product with long-document context needs. Discussed tradeoffs between hosted/dedicated/private, model choices (Llama2, Mistral, Falcon), context lengths 32k vs 100k+, and tool/function calling + retrieval. Agreed to share security docs and run a benchmark POC.

[00:00] Sam Lee (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'm Sam from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Miguel (CTO): good, thanks. Excited to chat. We're evaluating options for model selection and deployment mode.
[00:12] Priya Rao (Redwood SE): great, quick agenda: learn about your stack, context lengths, multilingual needs, any tool-calling/agent stuff, and then go over which open models line up and tradeoffs for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:20] Daniel (Product): sounds good. I'll chime in on UX constraints.

[00:35] Aisha (ML Eng): quick intro—Cerulean builds a compliance assistant that ingests long contracts, multi-lang (EN/ES/JP primarily), and calls out to backend services for lookups, so we need function-calling/tool support. We're exploring open models to avoid vendor lock and cost levers.
[00:50] Lina (Security): and security is big—SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS, and data residency are must-haves for some customers.

[01:05] Sam Lee: perfect. on the model side, are you leaning towards any particular families? we've seen a lot of customers compare Llama 2 derivatives, Mistral, Falcon, and some are testing the newer 65k/100k context variants.
[01:18] Miguel: we did a quick prototype with Llama2-70b and liked the latency but saw hallucinations on long docs. Aisha ran Mistral and it was cheaper but struggled on Japanese. So it's kind of mixed.

[01:40] Priya: yeah, language coverage can vary—some Mistral weights are optimized for code/English. Falcon has good instruction-following but can be heavy on cost. Also worth noting context windows: Llama2 forks often have 32k variants, there are experimental 65k or 100k models from other vendors but availability and stability differ.
[01:58] Aisha: our biggest question is, for 50–100k token documents, do we need a specialized long-context model or can we stitch with retrieval/kv cache?

[02:15] Priya: good question. we usually recommend a hybrid: use a model with as large a native context as feasible (e.g., 32k) and combine with retrieval and KV caching for the rest. Redwood supports automatic prefix KV cache and streaming so you can preserve latency while keeping cost down.
[02:34] Miguel: how reliably does the KV cache work with ephemeral sessions? we have multi-tenant flows and privacy concerns.
[02:43] Priya: KV cache is per-session/namespace and can be configured with retention policies. For Private deployments you can keep all caches on-prem, and for Dedicated we offer tenancy isolation and data routing policies. There was a little audio note: sometimes transcript labels KV "cash" in auto transcribe.

[03:05] Daniel: function calling — we need structured tool-calling: call our contract DB, run a clause-extraction microservice, and then update our ticketing system. How do Redwood's APIs support that?
[03:18] Sam Lee: our generation API supports structured function calling exactly—it's compatible with common function schemas, returns structured outputs, includes retry/fallback policies, and we have examples in SDKs. Priya can share the code samples.
[03:30] Priya: once you define the function signatures we can route responses to your service endpoints, plus we support streaming and partial outputs so your UI can render progressively. There may be small JSON packing oddities at first in the transcript as the auto-transcribe sometimes mis-parses.

[03:49] Lina: on security, SOC2 and encryption—do you have KMS/HSM integration and can we bring our own keys?
[03:56] Priya: yes, BYOK is supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations with restrictions. We also produce audit logs for all requests and have role-based access controls and SSO (SAML/OIDC). We'll share more in the security pack.

[04:18] Miguel: great. cost/latency story—if we go hosted and use a 32k model vs Dedicated with quantized 70b, what are we looking at for average latency and cost per request?
[04:30] Priya: rough rules of thumb—small-medium models on hosted are lowest ops friction, latency depends on batch size and streaming. Dedicated lets you pin GPU types, use quantization to reduce cost per token and lower tail latency. We'll send a sizing spreadsheet but expect Dedicated to have better predictable p99 latencies for high throughput.

[04:55] Aisha: multilingual—how do you evaluate models for Japanese/Spanish? do you benchmark on our data?
[05:02] Sam Lee: we typically run targeted evals—redwood Optimize can run prompt-sensitivity tests across candidate models. For POC we recommend you provide a sample set (Aisha volunteered). We'll run side-by-side on your prompts and metrics like exact match, hallucination rate, and token cost.

[05:20] Miguel: about model variants—do you support serving multiple compatible variants and automatic fallback? e.g., if high load, fallback from 100k variant to 32k plus retrieval?
[05:28] Priya: yes, smart routing and fallback policies are built into the platform. You can define policies to route by latency, cost, or region; we can also automatic fallback to quantized or smaller variants when capacity is constrained.

[05:46] Daniel: any gotchas with function calling when models are quantized or lower precision? We saw some schema mismatch in earlier tests.
[05:54] Priya: function-calling is generally robust but quantization can slightly affect tokenization and generation quality; we recommend a small validation set after quantization. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization levels per workload.

[06:12] Aisha: for very long contexts (100k+), are there open models you recommend now, or should we wait for more mature 100k+ weights?
[06:22] Priya: a few newer forks and research models are experimenting with 100k+, but maturity varies. Practically, hybrid retrieval + 32k models is the most stable approach today. If your workflow absolutely needs a single 100k window, we can scope a POC to test the newest long-context weights from the open community, but SLA and performance may be less predictable.

[06:45] Miguel: ok — thinking about deployment mode: our prioritized customers need data residency and strict SOC2 controls; might be leaning Private. But we want to understand incremental cost vs Dedicated.
[06:58] Sam Lee: that makes sense. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control for residency and key management, higher fixed platform fee and possible on-prem packaging costs. Dedicated gives isolation and predictable throughput with lower upfront platform fee, but keys may be managed through your cloud KMS. We'll detail the tradeoffs in the pricing doc.

[07:20] Lina: any compliance attestations we should know about beyond SOC2—ISO, FedRAMP?
[07:25] Priya: we have SOC2 Type II; ISO is in progress; FedRAMP is not currently offered. For sensitive workloads we advise Private deployments where you control the environment.

[07:40] Miguel: curious about benchmark cadence—what do you need from us to run the eval?
[07:46] Priya: a representative sample set (Aisha to provide), expected input/output schema, preferred metrics (latency, accuracy, hallucination), and access details if we run in your VPC or with sample data. We'll run against candidate open models and a Hosted Redwood baseline.

[08:05] Aisha: we'll provide a few hundred documents and example queries.

[08:10] Daniel: timeline—targeting a pilot in mid-Oct, decision by end of Oct.

[08:15] Sam Lee: sounds good. we'll follow up with a pricing spreadsheet, security pack, and schedule the technical deep dive.

[08:24] Miguel: quick question on multi-tenancy: can Dedicated support strict tenant isolation? we need per-tenant RBAC and separate billing.

[08:31] Priya: Dedicated supports tenancy isolation and per-route quotas; you can enforce per-tenant RBAC and we can export cost breakdowns per API key or token. For strictest isolation you'd consider Private.

[08:45] Daniel: any pitfalls migrating from an OpenAI-based flow to Redwood hosted—esp around API compatibility?

[08:52] Sam Lee: our API is designed to be developer-friendly; we provide migration guides and adapter samples. Function-calling schemas and streaming have slightly different shapes across vendors so expect some mapping.

[09:06] Aisha: just to call out, we need deterministic outputs for some compliance checks; how do you handle seed/control?

[09:12] Priya: determinism is tough at scale. we offer temperature controls, top-p, and sampling options, plus we can pin model versions and snapshot prompts/contexts for audits. For guaranteed determinism you may need a non-sampling setup and rigorous validation.

[09:30] Miguel: ok let's recap and next steps.

[09:33] Sam Lee: recap: 1) Cerulean needs long-document, multilingual, function-calling. 2) Recommended path — start with a hybrid approach: 32k models + retrieval/KV cache and run side-by-side evals on candidate open models (Llama2 variants, Mistral, Falcon). 3) We'll share security docs and pricing, and schedule a 2-hour technical benchmark in week of Oct 13.

[09:55] Aisha: that matches. I'll drop sample data and prompts by Oct 8.
[09:58] Miguel: we'll wait for the pricing and security pack. Thanks.

[10:05] Sam Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the docs and a calendar invite for the deep dive.

End of transcript.
